title: Invertibility of an existing linear strict-local comparison
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point with algebraically closed $\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Put $Z=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{sh}_{Y,s})$ and $p:Z\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Let $J$ be the small model of ring-written affine pointed neighbourhoods of $s$, and $B:J\to X_{et}$ their base-change diagram. For $j\in J$, let $\delta_j:Z\to p^{-1}B_j$ be the graph of the strict-henselization limit leg after the pullback symmetry. Define $r_j:F(B_j)\to\Gamma(Z,p^{-1}F)$ as the adjunction unit at $B_j$, restriction along $\delta_j$, and the inverse terminal-section/global-section isomorphism. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $a:(f_*F)_s\to\Gamma(Z,p^{-1}F)$ be a linear map [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] such that $\operatorname{germ}_j\,;a=r_j$ for every $j\in J$. Then $a$ is an isomorphism. This statement only proves invertibility of a given map; it neither constructs a map nor assumes existence of the comparison isomorphism.

proof.text: Base change Spec.map of the inverse canonical small/full ring-colimit isomorphism, using smallStrictLocalization_toBase, and compose with pullback symmetry. The resulting scheme isomorphism is over X, and its composite with each full-model leg equals pullback symmetry followed by the small-model leg, by the latter's definition.

Apply exists_moduleSectionsIsoTransport along this isomorphism, obtaining a bijection from the given target module to the full-model terminal set sections and the formula for each neighbourhood restriction. The forgetful functor preserves the relevant filtered colimits; sheafFiberCompIso supplies the source bijection and its germ formula.

Apply the uniqueness clause of the official sets_pushforward_stalk_strictHenselization theorem to the conjugated given map. The assumed representative equation, coefficient-forgetting germ identity, and transported graph formula verify its hypotheses. The canonical set map is bijective. Cancel the source and target bijections using Mathlib Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff and Equiv.comp_bijective; the concrete-category criterion proves the given module map is an isomorphism.
